partners.mechanism_chain: SPRED1 variant (rs61754855) —DISRUPTS→ SPRED1 (HGNC:17091); SPRED1 (HGNC:17091) —DECREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402); HRAS (HGNC:4835) —INCREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402); NRAS (HGNC:7930) —INCREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402); PIK3CA (HGNC:9538) —INCREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402); FGFR3 (HGNC:3520) —INCREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402); RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402) —LEADS_TO→ Leopard syndrome 1 phenotype (HP:0001077); RAS signaling pathway (WP:WP402) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermal nevus phenotype (HP:0000983). Leopard syndrome 1 is caused by loss-of-function mutations in SPRED1, which normally acts as a negative regulator of the RAS signaling pathway. This loss of regulation leads to hyperactivation of RAS signaling. Epidermal nevi can be caused by somatic gain-of-function mutations in HRAS, NRAS, PIK3CA, or FGFR3, all of which are components or activators of the RAS signaling pathway. Thus, both conditions result from dysregulation of the same core signaling pathway, albeit through different primary genetic mechanisms (loss of negative regulation vs. gain of positive regulation), converging on hyperactivation of RAS signaling.
